# Adjudication Task — Chapter 236

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃236화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|사내는 가지런히 놓인 문방사우(文房四友)를 바라봤다.
  6|
  7|담비 털로 만든 붓, 벼루는 푸르스름한 옥이었고 먹과 종이는 만 리나 떨어진 해동의 왕실에서 쓰인다는 진상품이었다.
  8|
  9|하나같이 어지간한 부호가 아니고서야 쓸 수 없는 최상품들.
 10|
 11|“좋군, 좋아.”
 12|
 13|절로 흐뭇한 미소가 지어졌다. 검소하기로 유명한 사내가 유일하게 부리는 사치가 바로 이 문방사우였다.
 14|
 15|“자, 그럼 슬슬 시작해 볼까.”
 16|
 17|사내가 기분 좋게 먹을 갈던 그때, 문이 열리더니 한 사람이 거침없는 발걸음으로 다가왔다.
 18|
 19|“누가 보면 한림학사(翰林學士)인 줄 알겠습니다.”
 20|
 21|불청객의 정체는 먼지투성이 차림의 무인이었다.
 22|
 23|쭉 찢어진 눈매, 허리춤에는 손때 묻은 검을 찬 그를 본 사내가 짐짓 얼굴을 굳혔다.
 24|
 25|“한림학사라니. 차라리 대화백(大畫伯)이라 불러 주게.”
 26|
 27|“여전히 그림을 그리십니까?”
 28|
 29|“내 유일한 낙이라네.”
 30|
 31|“안타깝게도 대화백에 어울리는 풍채는 아닌 것 같습니다만. 저한테 무공 한 번 배워 보시렵니까?”
 32|
 33|“정중하게 거절하지. 무인으로서의 내 한계는 딱 여기까지야.”
 34|
 35|“저런. 무인이 가져야 할 소양이 부족하시군요.”
 36|
 37|“상관없네. 내 수하 중에 검을 아주 기가 막히게 쓰는 친구가 하나 있거든. 오죽하면 별호가 귀검이겠나.”
 38|
 39|사내의 능청스러운 태도에 불청객의 얼굴이 스르륵 풀어졌다.
 40|
 41|다음 순간, 두 사람은 약속이라도 한 것처럼 피식 실소를 흘렸다.
 42|
 43|“주군께서는 여전하십니다.”
 44|
 45|“위팽, 자네도.”
 46|
 47|자그마치 넉 달 만에 보는 얼굴이라 반가움은 더욱 컸다.
 48|
 49|태원 진가의 소가주, 진위경은 만면에 웃음을 띤 채 위팽의 어깨를 두드렸다.
 50|
 51|“이 사람, 연통도 없이 어쩐 일인가? 전서구에는 내일 정오에나 당도한다고 적혀 있던데.”
 52|
 53|“진룡대(進龍隊)는 저 없어도 잘 굴러갑니다.”
 54|
 55|진룡대는 현재 태원 진가를 대표하는 무력 집단이었다.
 56|
 57|창설된 지 고작 일 년밖에 되지 않았으나 개개인의 무위가 뛰어났고, 가문에 대한 충성심은 그 이상으로 높았다.
 58|
 59|진위경의 심복인 위팽이 진룡대의 대주를 맡은 것부터가 그 위상을 짐작게 했다.
 60|
 61|“대주씩이나 돼서 말도 없이 혼자 빠져나온 건 아니겠지?”
 62|
 63|“그럴 리가 있겠습니까. 혁가 놈에게 맡겨 뒀으니 알아서 잘 올 겁니다.”
 64|
 65|“임시 부대주 말인가?”
 66|
 67|“예.”
 68|
 69|“이번이 첫 임무였지. 곁에서 지켜보니 어떻던가?”
 70|
 71|순간 위팽의 눈썹이 움찔거렸다. 이제 어느 정도 익숙해졌다고 생각했는데, 놈을 생각하는 것만으로도 골이 아파 왔다.
 72|
 73|그래도 공은 공이고 사는 사다. 그는 한숨처럼 대답했다.
 74|
 75|“그럭저럭 쓸 만하더군요. 쉴 새 없이 주둥이를 나불거리는 것만 빼면 말입니다.”
 76|
 77|“대충 알고는 있었지만 생각보다 쾌활한 친구인가 보군.”
 78|
 79|“지랄 맞을 정도로 쾌활해서 문제지요.”
 80|
 81|“다른 부분은?”
 82|
 83|“……옆에서 하나씩 알려 주면 금방 배우긴 합니다.”
 84|
 85|“자네가 그렇게 말할 정도면 상당한 무재라는 소리지.”
 86|
 87|지금으로부터 일 년 전, 혁무진은 그간의 공로를 인정받아 진룡대에 들어가는 영광을 누렸다.
 88|
 89|물론 그러한 인사 결정에는 진태경의 입김도 한몫했다.
 90|
 91|
 92|
 93|‘그 녀석, 생각보다 괜찮은 놈입니다. 한번 키워 보세요.’
 94|
 95|
 96|
 97|아우들의 말이라면 껌뻑 죽는 진위경이다.
 98|
 99|혹시나 하는 마음에 진룡대에 넣고 위팽을 붙여 가르쳤더니 하루가 다르게 실력이 좋아지는 게 아닌가.
100|
101|성격이 능글맞아 대원들과도 잘 어울렸고, 충성심이야 말할 것도 없었다.
102|
103|“으하하! 역시 우리 막내가 사람 보는 눈이 있어.”
104|
105|호탕하게 웃은 진위경의 손에는 언제 꺼냈는지 모를 술병이 들려 있었다.
106|
107|한 잔 가득 따라 건네준 그가 입을 열었다.
108|
109|“여하간 고생 많았네. 그래, 이제 북부 고원 쪽은 다 정리된 건가?”
110|
111|“예. 적어도 향후 십 년간은 문제없을 겁니다.”
112|
113|북부 고원의 안정화.
114|
115|그것이 위팽이 지난 넉 달 동안 태원진가를 떠나 있었던 이유였다.
116|
117|진위경은 진정한 산서성의 패자가 되기 위해서는 고원의 마적들을 토벌해야 한다고 생각했고, 수개월의 은밀하고도 치밀한 준비 끝에 자신이 가진 가장 날카로운 병기를 놈들에게 휘둘렀다.
118|
119|귀검(鬼劍) 위팽이라는 검을.
120|
121|“일곱 갈래로 쳐들어가니 속수무책으로 허물어지더군요.”
122|
123|산서 무림은, 특히 주 피해 지역인 북부 지역의 문파와 상단은 태원진가의 용단에 감사를 표하며 적극적으로 협력했다.
124|
125|위팽과 진룡대를 선봉으로 한, 이른바 칠로군(七路軍)이 탄생했고 그들은 상단들의 전폭적인 지원 아래 질 좋은 병장기와 군마로 무장했다.
126|
127|거기에 더해 강력한 지원군도 참전했다.
128|
129|“하오문, 무섭더군요. 정보의 무서움을 다시 한번 실감했습니다.”
130|
131|종전 직후 북부의 이권을 상당 부분 할당받은 하오문은 진위경의 결정을 쌍수 들고 환영했다.
132|
133|그들은 숙련된 정보 상인답게 마적들의 일거수일투족을 감시하는 한편, 허위 정보를 흘리고 함정을 팠다.
134|
135|그 철두철미함에 진위경도 혀를 내두를 정도였다.
136|
137|“세상 모든 것은 주인에 따라 쓰임새가 달라지는 법. 진정 무서운 것은 월화라네. 산서성에만 머무를 그릇이 아니야.”
138|
139|“그렇습니까?”
140|
141|“결과를 보고도 모르겠나? 그녀의 진정한 무기는 아름다운 용모가 아니라 지략이라는 것을.”
142|
143|이천 명.
144|
145|그날 하루 북부 고원에서 죽거나 사로잡힌 마적의 숫자였다.
146|
147|각기 다른 장소에서 일곱 번의 전투가 일어났고, 일곱 번의 승리를 거머쥔 그들은 거침없이 진격했다.
148|
149|“그 후로는 닥치는 대로 죽이고 사로잡았습니다.”
150|
151|하늘에는 수백 마리의 까마귀가 날아다녔고, 그 아래에는 그 열 배는 됨직한 시신들이 굴러다녔다.
152|
153|칠로군의 말발굽이 멈췄을 때는 이미 다섯 개의 대형 마적단이 궤멸하고 열 개가 넘는 마적단이 항복한 후였다.
154|
155|“사실상 이미 목적을 이룬 것이나 다름없었지요.”
156|
157|“아직 하지 않은 이야기가 있는 것으로 아는데.”
158|
159|“아, 유목민들 말입니까?”
160|
161|“바로 맞췄네.”
162|
163|신속한 기동 타격 덕분에 피해는 적었지만, 칠로군은 연이은 전투로 상당한 피로가 누적되어 있었다.
164|
165|그러던 찰나 거대한 먼지구름과 함께 수천의 유목민들이 나타난 것이다.
166|
167|“사실 그때는 저도 눈앞이 아찔했습니다.”
168|
169|하나하나가 마상무예의 달인이라는 유목민족이 무려 수천이다.
170|
171|제아무리 위팽이 완숙한 절정 고수라 해도 홀로 전황을 뒤집을 방법은 없었다.
172|
173|“그때 앞서 전서로 보고드렸던 그 일이 벌어진 겁니다.”
174|
175|“스스로를 칸이라 칭했다는 그들 말인가?”
176|
177|한때 중원까지 지배했던 거대한 유목 제국이 까마득한 과거가 된 지 오래다. 그러나 정복자의 핏줄은 끊어지지 않았고 칸이라는 칭호 역시 마찬가지였다.
178|
179|“두 사람이었습니다. 그들이 먼저 나서 자신들을 소개하기를…….”
180|
181|“대칸의 후예이자 황금 씨족의 일원인 테무르와 칭겐.”
182|
183|“정확합니다.”
184|
185|위팽은 고개를 끄덕였다.
186|
187|각각 이천 명의 인마를 거느리고 온 초원의 젊은 부족장들은 공격적이지도, 거만하지도 않았다.
188|
189|오히려 서툰 한어(韓語)로 조심스럽게 대화를 시도해 왔다.
190|
191|
192|
193|‘당신들 중 태원진가에서 온 이가 있소?’
194|
195|
196|
197|예상했던 전투는 벌어지지 않았다. 다름 아닌 화왕 적천강의 이름 덕분이었다.
198|
199|“이미 고원에까지 소문이 퍼졌더군요. 그들은 이미 적 대협과 삼공자의 관계를 알고 있었고, 우리와 적대하고 싶지 않다고 했습니다.”
200|
201|“내가 궁금한 점이 그것일세. 화왕의 위명 하나만 보고 물러났다기에는 워낙 석연찮아.”
202|
203|“아, 그거 말입니까? 저도 영 찝찝하길래 포로로 잡은 마적단 놈들을 족쳐 봤습니다.”
204|
205|위팽이 씩 웃으며 말을 이었다.
206|
207|“작년 겨울에 혼쭐이 난 전력이 있더군요. 흑사와 인도라고, 고원에서 악명 높은 마적단 두목 놈들을 적 대협께서 일장에 쳐 죽였답니다. 그 자리에 두 사람도 있었고요.”
208|
209|“겁을 집어먹었군.”
210|
211|“한편으로는 도움도 받았습니다. 우두머리가 죽고 혼란에 빠진 마적 잔당들을 그대로 흡수해서 여기까지 컸으니 말입니다.”
212|
213|테무르와 칭겐은 운이 좋았다.
214|
215|흑사와 인도가 한 자리에서 죽고, 얼마 지나지 않아 천풍단마저 적천강의 손에 전멸하자 힘의 공백이 생긴 것이다.
216|
217|마적 잔당을 병탄하고 뿔뿔이 흩어진 유목민들을 끌어모은 그들은 불과 일 년 사이에 고원의 강자로 급부상했다.
218|
219|“앞으로는 친하게 지내잡니다. 노략한 금은보화에 모피도 잔뜩 실어 주던데요.”
220|
221|“뭐라? 으하하하!”
222|
223|진위경은 시원한 웃음을 터트렸다.
224|
225|더할 나위 없는 결과다.
226|
227|이번 토벌로 태원진가는 명성과 산서 무림에서의 입지를 더욱 단단히 굳힌 동시에, 산하 문파와 양민들의 지지를 얻게 되었으니까.
228|
229|“고생했네. 자네의 공이 커.”
230|
231|“그건 잘 모르겠고, 제 술잔이 빈 건 알겠습니다.”
232|
233|“하하, 오늘은 만취할 때까지 마셔 보세.”
234|
235|두 사람을 술잔을 주거니 받거니 하며 이야기를 나누었다.
236|
237|지난 일 년 사이 워낙 많은 일이 있었던 터라 이야깃거리는 많았다.
238|
239|“아 참, 성운표국은 어떻게 됐습니까?”
240|
241|“자네가 떠난 직후 완전히 마무리 지었지. 이제는 진가표국이라고 불러야겠지만.”
242|
243|성운표국의 국주인 우황태 일가는 푼돈만 챙긴 채 도망쳤다. 몇몇 관리를 매수하여 군수품을 뒤로 빼돌린 것이 드러난 것이다.
244|
245|그 과정에서 진태경의 열렬한 신봉자인 상산왕 주표가 큰 도움을 줬음은 물론이었다.
246|
247|“타 문파와의 연수도 순조롭네. 숭산을 거쳐 합비까지 떠나는 표행이 진행 중이야.”
248|
249|“숭산과 합비라면……?”
250|
251|“소림과 남궁. 좋은 제의라 거절할 이유가 없었네.”
252|
253|천하 무림의 태산북두인 소림과 오대세가 중에서도 수위에 꼽히는 남궁세가.
254|
255|워낙 그 규모가 거대하다 보니 거래를 트는 것만으로도 만족이었는데, 도리어 저쪽에서 먼저 거래를 제안해 왔다. 그것도 아주 후한 조건으로.
256|
257|“적 대협의 존재가 본가에 큰 도움이 되는군요.”
258|
259|위팽의 말에 진위경은 말없이 웃었다.
260|
261|적어도 무림에서만큼은 대가 없는 호의가 없다고 굳게 믿는 그였다.
262|
263|저들의 호의에는 두 사람분의 값이 들어가 있다.
264|

Having received a considerable share of the northern region’s interests immediately after the war, the Lower District Sect had welcomed Jin Wikyung’s decision with open arms.

[P65]
Like the seasoned information merchants they were, they monitored the mounted bandits’ every move while spreading false information and laying traps.

[P66]
Their thoroughness was enough to leave even Jin Wikyung shaking his head in admiration.

[P67]
“Everything in this world is put to different use depending on who wields it. The truly frightening one is Wolhwa. She isn’t meant to remain confined to Shanxi Province.”

[P68]
“Is that so?”

[P69]
“Can’t you tell from the results? Her true weapon isn’t her beauty. It’s her strategic mind.”

[P70]
Two thousand.

[P71]
That was the number of mounted bandits killed or captured in Northern Gaoyuan in that single day.

[P72]
Seven battles broke out in seven different locations. After claiming seven victories, the army advanced without hesitation.

[P73]
“After that, we killed or captured every mounted bandit we came across.”

[P74]
Hundreds of crows wheeled through the sky, while perhaps ten times as many corpses lay scattered across the ground below.

[P75]
By the time the Seven-Route Army’s horses finally came to a halt, five major mounted-bandit groups had been annihilated and more than ten others had surrendered.

[P76]
“We had effectively achieved our objective by then.”

[P77]
“I believe there’s more to the story.”

[P78]
“Ah. You mean the nomads?”

[P79]
“Exactly.”

[P80]
Thanks to their swift, mobile strikes, the Seven-Route Army had suffered few casualties. But the successive battles had left them thoroughly exhausted.

[P81]
That was when thousands of nomads appeared amid a massive cloud of dust.

[P82]
“To be honest, even my heart sank when I saw them.”

[P83]
There were thousands of them, and every one was said to be a master of mounted combat.

[P84]
No matter how seasoned a Peak master Wipeng was, he had no way to turn the tide of battle alone.

[P85]
“That was when the incident I reported earlier by messenger pigeon occurred.”

[P86]
“You mean the ones who called themselves khans?”

[P87]
The great nomadic empire that had once ruled even the Central Plains had long since faded into distant history. But the conquerors’ bloodline had not died out, and neither had the title of khan.

[P88]
“There were two of them. They came forward first and introduced themselves…”

[P89]
“Temur and Chinggen, descendants of the Great Khan and members of the Golden Clan.[^2]”

[P90]
“Exactly.”

[P91]
Wipeng nodded.

[P92]
The young chieftains of the steppe had each arrived with two thousand riders. They were neither aggressive nor arrogant.

[P93]
Instead, they cautiously attempted to converse in halting Han language.

[P94]
“Is there anyone among you from the Jin Family of Taiyuan?”

[P95]
The battle everyone had expected never took place.

[P96]
All because of the name of the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.

[P97]
“The rumor had already reached Gaoyuan. They knew about the relationship between Great Hero Jeok and the Third Young Master, and said they had no wish to become our enemies.”

[P98]
“That is precisely what puzzles me. It seems rather suspicious that they would back down merely because of the Fire King’s reputation.”

[P99]
“Ah, that? It didn’t sit right with me either, so I beat the truth out of the mounted-bandit prisoners.”

[P100]
Wipeng grinned as he continued.

[P101]
“They’d already been taught a harsh lesson last winter. Great Hero Jeok killed two notorious mounted-bandit leaders from Gaoyuan—Black Sand and the Human Butcher—with a single palm strike. Temur and Chinggen were both there.”

[P102]
“So they were terrified.”

[P103]
“On the other hand, it benefited them as well. Once the leaders were dead, the mounted-bandit remnants fell into chaos. Temur and Chinggen absorbed them and grew as powerful as they are now.”

[P104]
Temur and Chinggen had been lucky.

[P105]
Black Sand and the Human Butcher had died in the same place, and not long afterward, the Heavenly Wind Band had also been annihilated by Jeok Cheongang. A power vacuum formed.

[P106]
After swallowing up the mounted-bandit remnants and gathering the scattered nomads, the two men had risen to become powers in Gaoyuan in the span of only a year.

[P107]
“They said they wanted to remain on friendly terms from now on. They even loaded us down with furs and plundered gold and silver.”

[P108]
“What? Ha-ha-ha!”

[P109]
Jin Wikyung burst into delighted laughter.

[P110]
The outcome could not have been better.

[P111]
The campaign had further strengthened the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s fame and standing in the Shanxi Murim while also winning the support of its affiliated sects and the common people.

[P112]
“You’ve worked hard. Much of the credit belongs to you.”

[P113]
“I don’t know about that, but I do know my cup is empty.”

[P114]
“Ha-ha! Then let’s drink until we’re both thoroughly drunk tonight.”

[P115]
The two men traded cups and stories.

[P116]
So much had happened over the past year that they had no shortage of things to discuss.

[P117]
“Oh, right. What happened to the Seongun Escort Bureau?”

[P118]
“We finished dealing with it soon after you left. Though I suppose we should call it the Jin Family Escort Bureau now.”

[P119]
Woo Hwangtae, chief of the Seongun Escort Bureau, had fled with his family, taking only a paltry sum with them. It had been discovered that they had bribed several officials and secretly diverted military supplies.

[P120]
Prince Shangshan, Zhu Bao, an ardent admirer of Jin Taekyung, had of course provided considerable help during the process.

[P121]
“Our cooperation with the other sects is progressing smoothly as well. An escort caravan traveling through Mount Song to Hefei is already under way.”

[P122]
“Mount Song and Hefei…?”

[P123]
“Shaolin and Namgung. It was too good an offer to refuse.”

[P124]
Shaolin, the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Murim, and the Nangong Family, counted among the foremost of the Five Great Families.

[P125]
Both were such enormous powers that Jin Wikyung would have been satisfied merely to establish trade with them. Instead, they had approached him first—and offered extremely generous terms at that.

[P126]
“Great Hero Jeok’s presence has been a tremendous help to our family.”

[P127]
Jin Wikyung merely smiled at Wipeng’s remark.

[P128]
He firmly believed that in the Murim, at least, no favor came without a price.

[P129]
Their generosity was an investment in two people.

[P130]
One was the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.

[P131]
The other was Jin Taekyung, the Sleeping Dragon.

[P132]
*Come to think of it, it’s already been a year since our youngest left.*

[P133]
It had been an eventful year.

[P134]
Once the ground thawed, the Star-Array Grand Banquet would be held in Henan. The brothers would meet again there.

[P135]
*Are you staying safe?*

[P136]
Jin Wikyung raised his cup, thinking of his thoughtless youngest brother, who had not contacted him even once. Just then, Wipeng spoke.

[P137]
“By the way, what were you planning to paint this time?”

[P138]
“I wonder.”

[P139]
“You were grinding ink without even deciding what to paint?”

[P140]
“It happens from time to time. I often spend one or two shichen grinding ink, only to put everything away again.”

[P141]
“Huh. Are you truly trying to become a master painter now?”

[P142]
“Put that thought aside for the moment. But once this painting is complete, I think I might deserve the title.”

[P143]
“Didn’t you just say you hadn’t decided what to paint?”

[P144]
“It’s merely that I can’t quite picture what it will look like. I decided on the title long ago.”

[P145]
“Then what is this magnificent work called?”

[P146]
Jin Wikyung answered with a smile.

[P147]
“The Sleeping Dragon Enters Service.”

[P148]
* * *

[P149]
He was a young man dressed in rags.

[P150]
His long, loose hair reached his shoulder blades, and thick stubble covered his chin and upper lip.

[P151]
The crowning touch was the iron balls dangling from all four limbs, making him look like a convict in a forced-labor camp.

[P152]
Yet one thing about him was different.

[P153]
His eyes.

[P154]
The young man stared into the blue-white flame with a gaze of unfathomable depth, then muttered,

[P155]
“Ah. This would be the perfect place to grill some meat.”

[P156]
The next instant—

[P157]
Fwoosh! Smack!

[P158]
With a savage crack of displaced air, a wrinkled palm slammed into the back of the young man’s head.

[P159]
“What an insolent brat! How dare you even think of grilling meat over our sect’s sacred flame!”

[P160]
The old man was beside himself with rage, but the young man merely grumbled.

[P161]
“Ah, why not? It should be fine if I just stick it in for a second and pull it right back out.”

[P162]
“What did you say?”

[P163]
“You’ve never heard of kiln-roasted pork belly? It’s insanely good.”

[P164]
“You—you’re dead today!”

[P165]
Smack! Crash!

[P166]
On an early spring day, as the earth thawed and fresh shoots poked their heads aboveground, peaceful Mount Jiuhua began to grow noisy.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 236

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃236화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|사내는 가지런히 놓인 문방사우(文房四友)를 바라봤다.
  6|
  7|담비 털로 만든 붓, 벼루는 푸르스름한 옥이었고 먹과 종이는 만 리나 떨어진 해동의 왕실에서 쓰인다는 진상품이었다.
  8|
  9|하나같이 어지간한 부호가 아니고서야 쓸 수 없는 최상품들.
 10|
 11|“좋군, 좋아.”
 12|
 13|절로 흐뭇한 미소가 지어졌다. 검소하기로 유명한 사내가 유일하게 부리는 사치가 바로 이 문방사우였다.
 14|
 15|“자, 그럼 슬슬 시작해 볼까.”
 16|
 17|사내가 기분 좋게 먹을 갈던 그때, 문이 열리더니 한 사람이 거침없는 발걸음으로 다가왔다.
 18|
 19|“누가 보면 한림학사(翰林學士)인 줄 알겠습니다.”
 20|
 21|불청객의 정체는 먼지투성이 차림의 무인이었다.
 22|
 23|쭉 찢어진 눈매, 허리춤에는 손때 묻은 검을 찬 그를 본 사내가 짐짓 얼굴을 굳혔다.
 24|
 25|“한림학사라니. 차라리 대화백(大畫伯)이라 불러 주게.”
 26|
 27|“여전히 그림을 그리십니까?”
 28|
 29|“내 유일한 낙이라네.”
 30|
 31|“안타깝게도 대화백에 어울리는 풍채는 아닌 것 같습니다만. 저한테 무공 한 번 배워 보시렵니까?”
 32|
 33|“정중하게 거절하지. 무인으로서의 내 한계는 딱 여기까지야.”
 34|
 35|“저런. 무인이 가져야 할 소양이 부족하시군요.”
 36|
 37|“상관없네. 내 수하 중에 검을 아주 기가 막히게 쓰는 친구가 하나 있거든. 오죽하면 별호가 귀검이겠나.”
 38|
 39|사내의 능청스러운 태도에 불청객의 얼굴이 스르륵 풀어졌다.
 40|
 41|다음 순간, 두 사람은 약속이라도 한 것처럼 피식 실소를 흘렸다.
 42|
 43|“주군께서는 여전하십니다.”
 44|
 45|“위팽, 자네도.”
 46|
 47|자그마치 넉 달 만에 보는 얼굴이라 반가움은 더욱 컸다.
 48|
 49|태원 진가의 소가주, 진위경은 만면에 웃음을 띤 채 위팽의 어깨를 두드렸다.
 50|
 51|“이 사람, 연통도 없이 어쩐 일인가? 전서구에는 내일 정오에나 당도한다고 적혀 있던데.”
 52|
 53|“진룡대(進龍隊)는 저 없어도 잘 굴러갑니다.”
 54|
 55|진룡대는 현재 태원 진가를 대표하는 무력 집단이었다.
 56|
 57|창설된 지 고작 일 년밖에 되지 않았으나 개개인의 무위가 뛰어났고, 가문에 대한 충성심은 그 이상으로 높았다.
 58|
 59|진위경의 심복인 위팽이 진룡대의 대주를 맡은 것부터가 그 위상을 짐작게 했다.
 60|
 61|“대주씩이나 돼서 말도 없이 혼자 빠져나온 건 아니겠지?”
 62|
 63|“그럴 리가 있겠습니까. 혁가 놈에게 맡겨 뒀으니 알아서 잘 올 겁니다.”
 64|
 65|“임시 부대주 말인가?”
 66|
 67|“예.”
 68|
 69|“이번이 첫 임무였지. 곁에서 지켜보니 어떻던가?”
 70|
 71|순간 위팽의 눈썹이 움찔거렸다. 이제 어느 정도 익숙해졌다고 생각했는데, 놈을 생각하는 것만으로도 골이 아파 왔다.
 72|
 73|그래도 공은 공이고 사는 사다. 그는 한숨처럼 대답했다.
 74|
 75|“그럭저럭 쓸 만하더군요. 쉴 새 없이 주둥이를 나불거리는 것만 빼면 말입니다.”
 76|
 77|“대충 알고는 있었지만 생각보다 쾌활한 친구인가 보군.”
 78|
 79|“지랄 맞을 정도로 쾌활해서 문제지요.”
 80|
 81|“다른 부분은?”
 82|
 83|“……옆에서 하나씩 알려 주면 금방 배우긴 합니다.”
 84|
 85|“자네가 그렇게 말할 정도면 상당한 무재라는 소리지.”
 86|
 87|지금으로부터 일 년 전, 혁무진은 그간의 공로를 인정받아 진룡대에 들어가는 영광을 누렸다.
 88|
 89|물론 그러한 인사 결정에는 진태경의 입김도 한몫했다.
 90|
 91|
 92|
 93|‘그 녀석, 생각보다 괜찮은 놈입니다. 한번 키워 보세요.’
 94|
 95|
 96|
 97|아우들의 말이라면 껌뻑 죽는 진위경이다.
 98|
 99|혹시나 하는 마음에 진룡대에 넣고 위팽을 붙여 가르쳤더니 하루가 다르게 실력이 좋아지는 게 아닌가.
100|
101|성격이 능글맞아 대원들과도 잘 어울렸고, 충성심이야 말할 것도 없었다.
102|
103|“으하하! 역시 우리 막내가 사람 보는 눈이 있어.”
104|
105|호탕하게 웃은 진위경의 손에는 언제 꺼냈는지 모를 술병이 들려 있었다.
106|
107|한 잔 가득 따라 건네준 그가 입을 열었다.
108|
109|“여하간 고생 많았네. 그래, 이제 북부 고원 쪽은 다 정리된 건가?”
110|
111|“예. 적어도 향후 십 년간은 문제없을 겁니다.”
112|
113|북부 고원의 안정화.
114|
115|그것이 위팽이 지난 넉 달 동안 태원진가를 떠나 있었던 이유였다.
116|
117|진위경은 진정한 산서성의 패자가 되기 위해서는 고원의 마적들을 토벌해야 한다고 생각했고, 수개월의 은밀하고도 치밀한 준비 끝에 자신이 가진 가장 날카로운 병기를 놈들에게 휘둘렀다.
118|
119|귀검(鬼劍) 위팽이라는 검을.
120|
121|“일곱 갈래로 쳐들어가니 속수무책으로 허물어지더군요.”
122|
123|산서 무림은, 특히 주 피해 지역인 북부 지역의 문파와 상단은 태원진가의 용단에 감사를 표하며 적극적으로 협력했다.
124|
125|위팽과 진룡대를 선봉으로 한, 이른바 칠로군(七路軍)이 탄생했고 그들은 상단들의 전폭적인 지원 아래 질 좋은 병장기와 군마로 무장했다.
126|
127|거기에 더해 강력한 지원군도 참전했다.
128|
129|“하오문, 무섭더군요. 정보의 무서움을 다시 한번 실감했습니다.”
130|
131|종전 직후 북부의 이권을 상당 부분 할당받은 하오문은 진위경의 결정을 쌍수 들고 환영했다.
132|
133|그들은 숙련된 정보 상인답게 마적들의 일거수일투족을 감시하는 한편, 허위 정보를 흘리고 함정을 팠다.
134|
135|그 철두철미함에 진위경도 혀를 내두를 정도였다.
136|
137|“세상 모든 것은 주인에 따라 쓰임새가 달라지는 법. 진정 무서운 것은 월화라네. 산서성에만 머무를 그릇이 아니야.”
138|
139|“그렇습니까?”
140|
141|“결과를 보고도 모르겠나? 그녀의 진정한 무기는 아름다운 용모가 아니라 지략이라는 것을.”
142|
143|이천 명.
144|
145|그날 하루 북부 고원에서 죽거나 사로잡힌 마적의 숫자였다.
146|
147|각기 다른 장소에서 일곱 번의 전투가 일어났고, 일곱 번의 승리를 거머쥔 그들은 거침없이 진격했다.
148|
149|“그 후로는 닥치는 대로 죽이고 사로잡았습니다.”
150|
151|하늘에는 수백 마리의 까마귀가 날아다녔고, 그 아래에는 그 열 배는 됨직한 시신들이 굴러다녔다.
152|
153|칠로군의 말발굽이 멈췄을 때는 이미 다섯 개의 대형 마적단이 궤멸하고 열 개가 넘는 마적단이 항복한 후였다.
154|
155|“사실상 이미 목적을 이룬 것이나 다름없었지요.”
156|
157|“아직 하지 않은 이야기가 있는 것으로 아는데.”
158|
159|“아, 유목민들 말입니까?”
160|
161|“바로 맞췄네.”
162|

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
